notes.title: Revelation of Decay Demo Returns, with More New Content!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! Long time no see and we’re back with a brand new demo!

In the previous open demo test, we received a ton of valuable feedback. We fully realize that a playable demo is the fastest way to communicate with players. But it took longer than expected to address everyone’s feedback, especially on tutorials, interaction, and other overall flow and underlying framework issues. Thanks a lot for your patience!

This new demo unlocks almost all content from two major early-game maps: Savage Outskirts and No.6 Middle School. You can now uncover the secrets hidden behind the school. We’ve also added more types of enemies, new bosses, and more weapons. Get ready to fight to your heart’s content!

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/5177d2b045b0f00ddab67b7d8f33c0f8eca25329.png
This version is much closer to our definition of a demo: approachable gameplay that’s easy to understand, plus new content that can keep you engaged for a good stretch of time. Therefore, the demo will be available for longer this time. If you can’t play right away, don’t worry! The test is planned to last until early October. During this period, we’ll continue to read your feedback and keep updating the demo.


Player-Friendly Early-Game Guidance

In earlier versions, many of you mentioned that the tutorial felt tedious and the guidance wasn’t clear. We’ve specifically redesigned the tutorial and map flow to make it easier to grasp game systems. We’ve also added tutorials for crafting medicine, cooking, and other activities to help make it clear how to survive and be stronger. 

Enemy distribution and map boundaries have also been adjusted, making the pace smoother and tighter overall. We hope newcomers can pick up the game more quickly, while veteran players still find fresh experiences in the familiar wasteland.

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/f24c9c3bcdb02de721615cbed0aa41cb9c5ec806.png
Building Base in Bizarre Zone 

Brightness and color tone in the Bizarre Zone were frequently brought up in feedback, so we gave the area a full makeover with freer entry and exit, clearer visuals, plus improved layout and animal behavior. It’s now a proper safehouse you can manage and explore. 

New facilities are added, including the fridge, pasture, and dismantling station. The workbench can now be upgraded and do automatic crafting. As the level rises, production becomes more efficient, pushing your base toward industrialization.

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/576995515cfff9db64718334e64ef5c98df373d4.png
Improved Controls & Visual Upgrades

For convenience, we added custom key binding so you can remap controls to your liking. We also addressed the issue that holding Shift to run felt awkward. Now you can now choose between Press to toggle walk/run or Hold to run. 

We also optimized lighting effects and environmental details, further improving the visual atmosphere and enhancing immersion in this apocalyptic adventure.


Also, Revelation of Decay has recently been selected for Convergence Showcase and Indie Fan Fest. There will be a gameplay video with my own commentary. If you’re interested, feel free to check it out!


And of course, the demo may still have some unknown bugs. If you encounter any issues during play, you can join our official Discord to report directly to me. I’ll fix them as soon as possible! If you’re interested in the game’s future, please add Revelation of Decay to your wishlist to stay tuned.

notes.title: Dev Blog #3: Bizarre Zone Rework & New WIP Area Snowfield
notes.content:
Hey everyone!
It’s been over a month since our last public demo, and during that time, we’ve been hard at work digesting all the feedback you gave us. In particular, issues like the Bizarre Zone being too dark or the survival difficulty feeling a bit overwhelming were already mentioned in the last blog, and now we’ve made visible progress addressing them.
Meanwhile, development of new maps and content hasn’t slowed down either. So today we’re sharing a bit of everything we’ve been working on!

Bizarre Zone – Visual Overhaul
Previously, we noted how the distorted, psychedelic visuals of the Bizarre Zone were negatively impacting the player experience. To address this, we’ve reworked the area’s lighting and color grading to create a clearer, more comfortable visual atmosphere.

We increased the overall brightness in both the Bizarre Zone and nighttime scenes, and revamped the lighting: instead of having light sources illuminating a circular area, now all reachable areas are properly illuminated. Also, the player character now carries a torch by default, illuminating nearby areas. The visual distortion effect has been removed as well.
Check the new Bizarre Zone and let us know if it feels improved!

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/ea2f9d71fe9de2895ad58c6131aa9d055741a64e.png
Survival Rebalance – More Guns
We've heard your feedback about the high survival pressure in the demo, especially with limited and underwhelming weapon options. Getting surrounded by hordes at night was frustrating for many. We've been thinking about how to balance the overall gameplay while still keeping the post-apocalyptic tension.

In line with the motto: “All fear comes from a lack of firepower”, we’ve decided to crank up the arsenal😂:
We buffed some melee weapons, improving their attack power and armor break, and added a few better melee options for early game. Most importantly, we’ve gone full arms dealer: over a dozen new firearms have been added, including the AWM, Barrett, and more. Pick your favorite!

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/be586968f3dfe05f46a73dc886e73c9ab0c4fb63.gif

New Area in Development - Snowfield
Stronger weapons mean new challenges! While the demo mostly showcased the Forest region, our full vision includes eight distinct biomes, each with unique terrain and enemy designs.
We’ve been pouring our creativity into the Snowfield, a classic survival game environment, with plenty of fresh content:
Common enemies like zombies in the Snowfield get new outfits (definitely unnecessary but did it anyway). New region-specific monsters are added, including Frost Insects, Corrupted Werewolves, and Giant White Bears. 

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/e44fe2528ebb5cf6dcecd71b8242e4f171ea2d5d.jpg
Since we noticed players in the demo loved raiding military bases, we’ve added various sizes of them to the Snowfield as well. Of course, expect resistances, there will be drones, turrets, and mechs guarding the loot.

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/4bf757d21c5d004208c1a0004db5bad61c513a49.jpg
As always, feel free to leave your thoughts and feedback in our official Discord server. We'll continue working hard to polish the game with your feedback!

By the way, we're invited to the BitSummit indie game festival in Kyoto, Japan! From July 18 to 20, Revelation of Decay will have its own booth at IP2-07, feel free to drop by and say hi!

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/bbd34f7623e0c83d9b348b8e6120c8a5434f3500.png

notes.title: Dev Blog #2: Survival&Combat Experience Optimization, and Reworked Bizarre Zone
notes.content:
Hello everyone! Last weekend, we wrapped up the first public playtest of "Revelation of Decay." We were truly flattered that over 20,000 players took the time to experience our demo and provide valuable feedback during the Steam Next Fest, despite so many other excellent demos available.

This past week, our team has been focused on reviewing hundreds of surveys submitted by you and brainstorming potential solutions. Many of the surveys included lengthy, detailed comments that provided us with numerous new ideas. Thank you so much for your participation and support! In this dev blog, we will share our updated development direction based on your feedback.

Revamping the bizarre zone visual
"Revelation of Decay" is a zombie game with supernatural powers, and the original intention behind the Bizarre Zone design was to immerse players in a mysterious, otherworldly atmosphere. We were trying to make it psychedelic and distorted in the hope of achieving this, but in practice, it ended up looking more like a view from someone who is drunk or "on that zaza".

It became clear: unless a game's art style is unique enough to justify player inconvenience, user experience (UX) often has priority.

Moving forward, we're considering a complete overhaul of the Bizarre Zone design. We'll make it more of an "easter egg" or part of exploration, rather than something mandatory. We'll also adjust the brightness and color scheme of its visuals, reduce or even remove the edge distortion effects, and ensure players automatically equip a torch upon entering the Bizarre Zone. We swear to protect your eyes going forward! 

Difficulty Rebalance
In a nutshell, the demo was all about two things: serving as an enemy punching bag and turning every single rock to find food that simply didn't exist. It’s just too hard to survive. 

We put in a lot of items and skills, just because they look fancy, into the early game, but not systems that genuinely enhance your survival and combat. Therefore, combat-related content will be a key focus for us moving forward. This means giving players more combat-beneficial equipment and dropping better weapons earlier. We want to avoid those moments where you grind your butt off only to get the Spiked Club that barely tickles enemies.

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45020835/7e09ac7c0ac87dae5f7f421ecd94575630b7c17e.jpg
However, even if you've got the gear, it's no good dealing with zombies on an empty stomach. While "Revelation of Decay" was not designed from the start to adopt a realistic and oppressive narrative tone, we included many nuanced elements such as the imbalance between food supply and stamina consumption, frequent random survival events, and a relatively fast enemy respawn rate. The accumulation of these factors ultimately led to significant pressure for players.

We don't intend to solve this by simply removing these survival elements. On the contrary, these survival elements are what make this virtual world feel more alive and immersive. The real challenge for the team in the long run is figuring out how to balance them.

Satisfying the hoarders
As mentioned, most of our team members love hoarding junk and then crafting pointless stuff out of it. So we brainstormed and designed too many "cool" items in the early stages and crammed them all into the demo. Turns out, many players share this "hoarding" spirit and diligently search every corner, leading to backpack overload.

It's time for us to rein in our creative urges, reduce the variety and quantity of items, focus on quality over quantity, and also provide more ways to consume items. Some items intended for the mid-to-late game will only appear at appropriate times, no longer taking up your valuable early-game space.

Furthermore, many of you pointed out the inconvenience of managing items in and out of the Super Pickup Pack. This design was actually a bit of an inside joke, primarily intended to curb our own developer "hoarding" tendencies. The idea was that if you picked up too much, it would naturally prompt a trip back to camp for some inventory management. In hindsight, we realize we didn't fully think this through.

The Pickup Pack will soon feature an item panel, allowing you to view its contents without transferring them out one by one. Items inside will also be sorted by the order they were added, making it easier to grab recently picked-up loot.

Finally, we received a lot of feedback on the early-game tutorials. Fixing this will involve more underlying changes, so please bear with us and give us some more time. We'll continue to update you on the development progress and adjustments through future dev blogs. If you have any thoughts on this demo playtest or our new adjustments, please join our Discord server to reach us more quickly! See you next time!

notes.title: We Need Your Feedback, Demo Update & Shout to the MIX showcase
notes.content:
Hello, everyone! We just pushed out a new update that adds some dash-and-attack–related Bizzar Matters and addresses several gameplay-affecting issues you reported. Full patch notes at the end! If you run into any bugs during your playthrough, please join our Discord or leave a comment under our tweets to let us know, and we’ll sort it out as quickly as possible!



It’s been just over a week since the new demo went live. More than 10,000 players have tried out Revelation of Decay and added it to their wishlists, and many of you have already started asking for the full release. We also went to the MIX Summer Game Showcase and got feedback from players there as well. Thank you for your support!

For the past few months, our team has been focused on overhauling the game’s overall architecture and laying the groundwork for future features. Everyone on the team has tons of ideas, bringing both opportunities and challenges to the game’s design. This public demo is essentially a rough, early-stage mix of our core mechanics, helping us to set the course for the game’s development based on your feedback.

We’ve seen your feedback. Everything from early map layout and tutorial to color palette and brightness, the team is already brainstorming solutions. But we need more focused feedback from you all. That’s why we’ve put together a short survey. 

Take the survey here:👉 https://forms.gle/zcwchvreiTNd4Nb1A



It won’t take long to fill out. We really want to get to know how you truly feel during your playthrough. Especially, what moment made you want to put down the game? Your feedback, no matter how small, means the world to us. Thank you for taking the time!



V0.1.7 DEMO PATCH NOTES

New:

1. Added new Bizarre Matters related to dashing and attacking, such as Athletic Medal.

Fixes:

1. Fixed an issue where pressing E wouldn’t work if the mouse cursor was hovering over UI elements.

2. Fixed the problem where the “Security Guard” NPC wouldn’t give you the “Spiked Club Blueprint.”

Optimizations:

1. The first NPC in the main quest line no longer requires players to equip a gun, but simply having one.

2. Weird M16 can no longer be dismantled.

3. You can now raise your shield while using healing items.

4. Torches in your inventory will be auto-equipped.

5. The confirmation pop-up after healing progress reaches 100% has been removed.

6. Weapon upgrades now jump by +1 instead of +0.5.

7. Wooden Sticks and Iron-Plated Sticks now match the map’s level requirements.

8. Improved visibility on roads in the Bizarre Zone.

9. Tweaked the level design of the lab area.

10. Tweaked the quests related to the Super Pickup Pack.



As you can tell from the version number, the game is still in early development. After collecting your feedback, we’ll conduct a full review and fine-tune everything. The demo will close on June 22. After that, we’ll continue sharing our plans and development progress through regular Dev Blogs. We’d love to have you join our Discord to discuss the development with us. This’s the fastest way to stay in touch and help shape the game!



P.S. Here’s a snapshot of our booth from the MIX Summer Game Showcase.
